blocks.explanation: Dekhiye, yeh sawal \(i\) ki power simplify karne ka hai. Given sirf \(i^{9}\) hai, aur humein find yeh karna hai ke yeh chaar values \(1, i, -1, -i\) mein se kaun si hai. Sirf yeh chaar hi kyun? Kyun ke \(i\) ki powers aik cycle (chakkar) mein ghoomti hain: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\), aur \(i^5\) se wahi silsila dobara shuru ho jata hai, bilkul ghari ki sui ki tarah jo 12 ke baad phir 1 par aa jati hai. Plan: power 9 ko 4 se divide karenge. 4 ke multiple wala hissa 1 ban jayega, aur sirf remainder (baqi) faisla karega ke jawab kya hai.
steps:
Step 1: Power ko 4 se divide karein
\[9 = 4 \times 2 + 1\]
\[i^{9} = i^{8} \cdot i\]
Kyun: Exponent ka qanoon \(a^{m+n} = a^m \cdot a^n\) kehta hai ke jab powers jama ho rahi hon to hum unhein alag alag factors bana sakte hain. 9 ko 8 + 1 likh kar hum \(i^9\) ko do hisson mein tor dete hain: aik hissa \(i^8\) jo 4 ka multiple hai aur aasani se 1 ban jata hai, aur doosra bacha hua \(i\).

Step 2: \(i^{8}\) ki jagah 1 likhein
\[i^{8} = (i^{4})^{2}\]
\[= 1^{2} = 1\]
\[i^{9} = 1 \cdot i = i\]
Kyun: \(i^4 = 1\) hai, is liye \(i^8 = (i^4)^2 = 1^2\). Aur 1 ko jitni baar marzi multiply karein, 1 hi rehta hai. Is tarah 4 ke multiple wala poora hissa jawab par koi asar nahin daalta, aur sirf bacha hua \(i\) jawab ban jata hai.
Dhyan dein: 9 ko 4 se divide karne par quotient (2) aur remainder (1) aate hain. Jawab ke liye sirf remainder dekhna hai, quotient nahin. Bohat se students quotient dekh kar \(i^2\) likh dete hain, jo ghalat hai.

Tasdeeq:
Remainder 1 ho to jawab hamesha \(i\) hota hai: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^5 = i\), \(i^9 = i\). Hamara jawab isi pattern mein fit baithta hai, yani theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(i^{9} = i\) (cycle do poore chakkar laga kar wapas \(i\) par aa gaya)

blocks.explanation: Yeh bilkul part (i) jaisa sawal hai, sirf power bari hai. Humein \(i^{17}\) ko \(1, i, -1, -i\) mein se kisi aik value mein badalna hai. Formula yahan wahi cycle wala qaida hai: \(i^4 = 1\), is liye 4 ka har multiple 1 ban jata hai. Plan: 17 ko 4 se divide karke remainder dekhein; wohi batayega ke cycle mein hum kahan khare hain.
steps:
Step 1: Power ko 4 se divide karein
\[17 = 4 \times 4 + 1\]
\[i^{17} = i^{16} \cdot i\]
Kyun: Power mein se 4 ka sab se bara multiple (yahan 16) alag kar lete hain, kyun ke usi hisse ko hum 1 bana sakte hain. Baqi 1 power bachti hai, yani aik \(i\).

Step 2: \(i^{16}\) ki jagah 1 likhein
\[i^{16} = (i^{4})^{4} = 1^{4} = 1\]
\[i^{17} = 1 \cdot i = i\]
Kyun: Qanoon \((a^m)^n = a^{mn}\) se \(i^{16} = (i^4)^4\) likha, aur \(i^4 = 1\) hone ki wajah se yeh \(1^4 = 1\) ban gaya. Ab \(1 \cdot i\) sirf \(i\) hai.
Dhyan dein: \(i^{16}\) ko \(16i\) ya \(4i\) mat samjhein. Power ka matlab baar baar multiply karna hai, number se zarb dena nahin.

Tasdeeq:
Remainder 1 aaya, to jawab \(i^1 = i\) jaisa hi hona chahiye. Hamara jawab \(i\) hai, yani theek hai. Khud sochiye: \(i^{18}\) kya hoga? (Remainder 2, to \(-1\).)
blocks.final_answer: \(i^{17} = i\) (17 ka remainder 1 hai, is liye jawab \(i\))

blocks.explanation: Ab yahan ruk kar dekhiye: is baar base \(-i\) hai, sirf \(i\) nahin. Yahi farq is sawal ki asal baat hai. Given \((-i)^{19}\) hai aur humein isay simple value mein likhna hai. Tareeqa yeh hai ke \(-i\) ko do factors (hisson) mein toren: \(-i = (-1) \cdot i\). Phir dono ki power alag alag nikaalenge, kyun ke \((-1)\) ki power aur \(i\) ki power dono ke apne aasaan qaide hain. Aakhir mein dono results multiply kar denge.
steps:
Step 1: Minus sign ko alag karein
\[(-i)^{19} = ((-1) \cdot i)^{19}\]
\[= (-1)^{19} \cdot i^{19}\]
Kyun: Qanoon \((ab)^n = a^n b^n\) kehta hai ke product ki power lein to har factor ko wohi power lagti hai. Is se aik mushkil cheez do aasaan cheezon mein bant jati hai.

Step 2: \((-1)^{19}\) nikaalein
\[(-1)^{19} = -1\]
Kyun: \(-1\) ko \(-1\) se multiply karein to \(+1\), phir \(-1\) se to \(-1\); yani even (juft) power par \(+1\) aur odd (taaq) power par \(-1\). 19 odd hai, is liye \(-1\).

Step 3: \(i^{19}\) nikaalein
\[19 = 4 \times 4 + 3\]
\[i^{19} = i^{16} \cdot i^{3}\]
\[= 1 \cdot (-i) = -i\]
Kyun: \(i^{16} = (i^4)^4 = 1\), aur bachi hui power 3 hai. \(i^3 = i^2 \cdot i = (-1)i = -i\). Yani cycle mein teesri value \(-i\) hai.

Step 4: Dono results multiply karein
\[(-i)^{19} = (-1)(-i)\]
\[= i\]
Kyun: Minus ko minus se multiply karein to plus banta hai, is liye \((-1)(-i) = +i\).
Dhyan dein: Bohat se students \((-i)^{19}\) ko seedha \(-(i^{19})\) samajh lete hain. Odd power par yeh sahi nikalta hai, lekin even power par ghalat ho jata hai: \((-i)^2 = -1\), jab ke \(-(i^2) = +1\). Hamesha \((-1)\) ki power alag nikaalein.

Tasdeeq:
\(-i\) ki powers ka apna cycle hai: \((-i)^1 = -i\), \((-i)^2 = -1\), \((-i)^3 = i\), \((-i)^4 = 1\). 19 ka remainder 3 hai, aur is cycle ki teesri value \(i\) hai. Dono tareeqon se jawab aik hi aaya.
blocks.final_answer: \((-i)^{19} = i\) (minus ki odd power ne sign aik baar aur palat diya)

blocks.explanation: Yeh is sawal ka sab se tricky hissa hai, is liye dhyan se. Power negative bhi hai aur fraction bhi: \(-21/2\). Sab se pehle humein yeh pehchanna hai ke half power (\(1/2\)) ka matlab square root hai, aur \((-1)^{1/2} = \sqrt{-1} = i\), jo iota ki definition hai. Is liye hum expression ko \(i\) ki power mein badal lenge: \((-1)^{-21/2} = ((-1)^{1/2})^{-21} = i^{-21}\). Phir negative power ko positive banayenge, \(i^{21}\) ko cycle se simplify karenge, aur aakhir mein \(i\) ko denominator (neeche) se nikaalenge.
steps:
Step 1: Power ko \((1/2) \times (-21)\) likhein
\[(-1)^{-\frac{21}{2}} = \left((-1)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{-21}\]
\[= (\sqrt{-1})^{-21}\]
\[= i^{-21}\]
Kyun: \(-21/2\) ko hum \((1/2) \times (-21)\) likh sakte hain, aur \((a^m)^n = a^{mn}\). Half power ka matlab square root hai, aur definition se \(\sqrt{-1} = i\). Pehle square root lena hi kitab ka tareeqa hai, aur isi se sahi jawab aata hai.

Step 2: Power ko positive banayein
\[i^{-21} = \dfrac{1}{i^{21}}\]
Kyun: Qanoon \(a^{-n} = 1/a^{n}\): negative power ka matlab hai ke cheez neeche (denominator mein) chali jaye aur power positive ho jaye. Positive power ko cycle se simplify karna aasaan hai.

Step 3: \(i^{21}\) simplify karein
\[21 = 4 \times 5 + 1\]
\[i^{21} = (i^{4})^{5} \cdot i = i\]
Kyun: 4 ka multiple wala hissa \(i^{20} = (i^4)^5 = 1\) hai, aur remainder 1 ki wajah se sirf aik \(i\) bachta hai. Ab expression \(1/i\) ban gaya.

Step 4: Denominator se \(i\) nikaalein
\[\dfrac{1}{i} = \dfrac{1}{i} \cdot \dfrac{i}{i}\]
\[= \dfrac{i}{i^{2}} = \dfrac{i}{-1}\]
\[= -i\]
Kyun: Jawab ko simple complex number banane ke liye neeche \(i\) nahin rehna chahiye. Upar neeche \(i\) se multiply karne se value nahin badalti (\(i/i = 1\)), lekin neeche \(i^2 = -1\) aa jata hai jo aam real number hai. \(i\) ko \(-1\) se divide kiya to \(-i\).

Aam ghalti (Common mistake)
Pehle power \(-21\) mat lagayein: \(((-1)^{-21})^{1/2} = (-1)^{1/2} = i\) aa jata hai, jo alag (ghalat) value hai. Negative number ki fractional power mein tarteeb (order) se farq parta hai, is liye hamesha pehle \(-1\) ka square root lein, jaise kitab karti hai. Doosri aam ghalti: \(1/i\) ko \(i\) samajh lena. Yaad rakhiye, \(1/i = -i\) hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[i \cdot (-i) = -i^{2} = 1\]
Agar \(-i\) waqai \(1/i\) hai to \(i\) se multiply karke 1 aana chahiye, aur 1 hi aaya. Jawab theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \((-1)^{-\frac{21}{2}} = -i\) (pehle square root se \(i\) bana, phir power aur reciprocal ne isay \(-i\) kar diya)

blocks.prompt: 2 Prove that \(\overline{z} = z\) iff \(z\) is real.
blocks.explanation: Yeh proof ka sawal hai, aur is mein lafz "iff" bohat aham hai. "iff" ka matlab hai "if and only if" (agar aur sirf agar), yani humein do taraf saabit karna hai, jaise aik pul jo dono taraf se guzarne ke qabil ho: (a) agar \(\overline{z} = z\) ho to \(z\) real hai; (b) agar \(z\) real ho to \(\overline{z} = z\). Sirf aik taraf saabit karna adhoora jawab hai. Tool hum yeh use karenge: \(z = a + ib\) likhein; conjugate (ulta sign wala saathi) \(\overline{z} = a - ib\) hai; aur \(z\) real tab hota hai jab \(b = 0\) ho.
steps:
Step 1: \(z\) aur \(\overline{z}\) ko letters mein likhein
\[z = a + ib, \; a, b \in \mathbb{R}\]
\[\overline{z} = a - ib\]
Kyun: Har complex number ko is shakal mein likha ja sakta hai, is liye jo baat \(a\) aur \(b\) ke liye saabit hogi woh har complex number ke liye sach hogi. Conjugate sirf imaginary part ka sign badalta hai; real part waisa hi rehta hai, jaise real axis mein aaine ka aks.

Step 2 (hissa a): Farz karein \(\overline{z} = z\)
\[a - ib = a + ib\]
\[-ib - ib = 0\]
\[-2ib = 0\]
\[b = 0\]
Kyun: Dono taraf se \(a + ib\) minus kiya: \(a\) cancel ho gaya aur \(-ib - ib = -2ib\) bacha. \(-2i\) zero nahin hai, is liye dono taraf ko \(-2i\) se divide kar sakte hain, aur \(b = 0\) mil jata hai.

Step 3: Natija: \(z\) real hai
\[z = a + i(0) = a\]
Kyun: \(b = 0\) ka matlab imaginary part khatam. Ab \(z\) sirf real number \(a\) reh gaya. Pehli taraf saabit ho gayi.

Step 4 (hissa b): Farz karein \(z\) real hai
\[z = a + i(0) = a\]
\[\overline{z} = a - i(0) = a\]
\[\overline{z} = z\]
Kyun: Real number mein \(b = 0\) hota hai, aur 0 ka sign badalne se 0 hi rehta hai (\(-0 = 0\)). Is liye conjugate lene se kuch nahin badla. Doosri taraf bhi saabit.
Dhyan dein: Exam mein dono hisson ko (a) aur (b) ke label ke saath likhein, taake examiner ko saaf nazar aaye ke "iff" ki dono directions saabit ki gayi hain.

Step 5: Dono hisse jor dein
Hissa (a) ne saabit kiya "agar \(\overline{z} = z\) to \(z\) real", aur hissa (b) ne ulti taraf "agar \(z\) real to \(\overline{z} = z\)". Dono mil kar "iff" wala poora statement saabit karte hain.

Tasdeeq:
Misaal: \(z = 5\) ho to \(\overline{z} = 5\), barabar. Lekin \(z = 5 + 2i\) ho to \(\overline{z} = 5 - 2i\), jo \(z\) ke barabar nahin, kyun ke yahan \(b \ne 0\). Yani jab tak imaginary part hai, number apne aaine ke aks jaisa nahin hota.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\overline{z} = z\) tab aur sirf tab jab \(z\) real ho (yani real numbers hi woh numbers hain jo real axis ke aaine mein apni jagah par rehte hain).

blocks.explanation: Yeh "show that" yani proof ka sawal hai: humein koi number nahin nikaalna, balke dikhana hai ke left side aur right side barabar hain. \(\operatorname{Re}(z)\) ka matlab \(z\) ka real part hai: \(z = a + ib\) ho to \(\operatorname{Re}(z) = a\). Plan: left side mein \(z\) aur \(\overline{z}\) ki values daalenge, simplify karenge, aur dekhenge ke aakhir mein sirf \(a\) bachta hai. Is result ka faida: \(z\) aur us ka conjugate jama karne se imaginary hissa cancel ho jata hai.
steps:
Step 1: \(z = a + ib\) farz karein
\[z = a + ib\]
\[\overline{z} = a - ib\]
Kyun: Yeh general complex number hai, jo har \(z \in C\) ko represent karta hai. Conjugate mein sirf \(ib\) ka sign badalta hai.

Step 2: \(z\) aur \(\overline{z}\) ko add karein
\[z + \overline{z} = (a + ib) + (a - ib)\]
\[= 2a\]
Kyun: Real parts jama hue: \(a + a = 2a\). Imaginary parts \(+ib\) aur \(-ib\) aapas mein cancel ho gaye. Yahi is sawal ka asal nukta hai.

Step 3: 2 se divide karein
\[\dfrac{z + \overline{z}}{2} = \dfrac{2a}{2} = a\]
\[= \operatorname{Re}(z)\]
Kyun: \(2a/2 = a\), aur \(a\) hi \(z\) ka real part hai. Left side right side ke barabar ho gayi.

Tasdeeq:
Misaal \(z = 3 + 4i\): \((3 + 4i + 3 - 4i)/2 = 6/2 = 3\), aur \(3 + 4i\) ka real part waqai 3 hai. Khud sochiye: \(z = -2 + 7i\) ke liye kya aayega?
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\dfrac{z + \overline{z}}{2} = \operatorname{Re}(z)\) (number aur us ke conjugate ka average sirf real part deta hai).

blocks.explanation: Yeh bhi proof hai, part (i) ka jora. \(\operatorname{Im}(z)\) imaginary part hai, yani \(z = a + ib\) mein woh real number \(b\) jo \(i\) ke saath laga hai (\(i\) ke baghair). Pichle part mein jama karne se \(ib\) cancel hua tha; is baar minus karenge to ulta \(a\) cancel hoga aur \(ib\) bachega. Plan: \(z\) mein se \(\overline{z}\) minus karein, phir \(2i\) se divide karke sirf \(b\) tak pohanchein.
steps:
Step 1: \(z = a + ib\) farz karein
\[z = a + ib\]
\[\overline{z} = a - ib\]
Kyun: Complex number aur us ke conjugate ki general shakal; is se proof har \(z\) ke liye sach hoga.

Step 2: \(z\) mein se \(\overline{z}\) minus karein
\[z - \overline{z} = (a + ib) - (a - ib)\]
\[= a + ib - a + ib\]
\[= 2ib\]
Kyun: Bracket se pehle minus ho to andar ke dono signs badal jate hain: \(-(a - ib) = -a + ib\). Phir \(a - a = 0\) aur \(ib + ib = 2ib\).
Dhyan dein: Yahan sab se zyada ghalti yeh hoti hai ke students \(-(a - ib)\) ko \(-a - ib\) likh dete hain aur jawab zero aa jata hai. Bracket kholte waqt dono terms ka sign badlein.

Step 3: \(2i\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{z - \overline{z}}{2i} = \dfrac{2ib}{2i} = b\]
\[= \operatorname{Im}(z)\]
Kyun: Upar aur neeche dono mein \(2i\) common hai, cancel ho gaya, aur sirf \(b\) bacha, jo imaginary part hai.

Aam ghalti (Common mistake)
\(\operatorname{Im}(z)\) barabar \(b\) hai, \(ib\) nahin. Imaginary part khud aik real number hota hai; \(i\) sirf yeh batata hai ke yeh number kis direction (vertical axis) mein hai. Isi liye formula mein \(2i\) se divide karte hain, sirf 2 se nahin.

Tasdeeq:
Misaal \(z = 3 + 4i\): \(z - \overline{z} = (3 + 4i) - (3 - 4i) = 8i\), aur \(8i/(2i) = 4\). \(3 + 4i\) ka imaginary part waqai 4 hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\dfrac{z - \overline{z}}{2i} = \operatorname{Im}(z)\) (farq lene se real part cancel ho kar sirf imaginary part bachta hai).

blocks.explanation: Proof ka sawal. Pehle samajhte hain \(|z|\) kya hai: yeh modulus hai, yani Argand diagram par origin se point \(z\) tak ka faasla (distance), jaise naqshe par ghar se school ki seedhi doori. Formula: \(|a + ib| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) (Pythagoras theorem se). Yahan dono sides alag alag cheezein lagti hain, aik mein square hai aur doosri mein multiplication. Plan: dono sides ko alag alag simplify karenge aur dikhayenge ke dono \(a^2 + b^2\) ke barabar hain.
steps:
Step 1: \(z = a + ib\) farz karein
\[z = a + ib\]
\[\overline{z} = a - ib\]
Kyun: General shakal, taake proof har complex number ke liye ho.

Step 2: Left side
\[|z| = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}\]
\[|z|^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}\]
Kyun: Modulus ki definition lagayi, phir square kiya. Square root ka square karne se root khatam ho jata hai, jaise \((\sqrt{9})^2 = 9\).

Step 3: Right side
\[z \cdot \overline{z} = (a + ib)(a - ib)\]
\[= a^{2} - (ib)^{2}\]
\[= a^{2} - i^{2}b^{2}\]
\[= a^{2} + b^{2}\]
Kyun: Yeh shakal \((x + y)(x - y)\) wali hai, jis ka jawab \(x^2 - y^2\) hota hai; yahan \(x = a\) aur \(y = ib\). Phir \((ib)^2 = i^2 b^2\), aur \(i^2 = -1\) ki wajah se \(-i^2 b^2\) ban gaya \(+b^2\).
Dhyan dein: \((ib)^2\) ko \(ib^2\) mat likhein; square \(i\) aur \(b\) dono par lagta hai.

Step 4: Muqabla karein
\[|z|^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2} = z \cdot \overline{z}\]
Kyun: Dono sides ka jawab aik hi expression \(a^2 + b^2\) aaya, is liye dono barabar hain. Is ka matlab: kisi complex number ko us ke conjugate se multiply karein to hamesha aik positive real number milta hai.

Tasdeeq:
Misaal \(z = 3 + 4i\): \(|z| = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5\), to \(|z|^2 = 25\); aur \((3 + 4i)(3 - 4i) = 9 + 16 = 25\). Dono barabar hain.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(|z|^{2} = z \cdot \overline{z}\) (number ko conjugate se zarb dene se us ke faasle ka square milta hai, jo hamesha real hai).

blocks.explanation: Proof ka sawal, aur yeh part (iii) par khara hai. Pehle aik shart: \(z \ne 0\), kyun ke zero se divide nahin hota. Yahan humein \(1/z\) ko aisi shakal mein likhna hai jis ke neeche koi \(i\) na ho. Sawal yeh hai ke kis cheez se multiply karein? Jawab: conjugate \(\overline{z}\) se, kyun ke part (iii) ne dikhaya ke \(z\overline{z}\) real number \(|z|^2\) hai. Plan: \(1/z\) ke upar neeche \(\overline{z}\) se multiply karein, phir part (iii) ka result laga dein.
steps:
Step 1: Upar neeche \(\overline{z}\) se multiply karein
\[\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{1}{z} \cdot \dfrac{\overline{z}}{\overline{z}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\overline{z}}{z\overline{z}}\]
Kyun: \(\overline{z}/\overline{z} = 1\) hai, aur kisi cheez ko 1 se multiply karne se value nahin badalti; sirf shakal badalti hai. \(\overline{z}\) is liye chuna kyun ke \(z\overline{z}\) real number ban jata hai, aur hum yahi chahte hain.

Step 2: Part (iii) use karein
\[z\overline{z} = |z|^{2}\]
\[\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{\overline{z}}{|z|^{2}}\]
Kyun: Part (iii) hum pehle hi saabit kar chuke hain, is liye usay seedha use kar sakte hain. Proofs mein pichle saabit shuda results ka istemal bilkul jaiz hai.

Teaching note
Isi wajah se complex number se divide karte waqt hum hamesha denominator ke conjugate se multiply karte hain: \(\dfrac{1}{a + ib} = \dfrac{a - ib}{a^2 + b^2}\). Yeh formula Sawal 4 (multiplicative inverse) aur Sawal 5 (division) dono ki bunyaad hai, is liye isay achhi tarah yaad kar lein.

Tasdeeq:
Misaal \(z = 3 + 4i\): formula se \(1/z = (3 - 4i)/25\). Ab \((3 + 4i) \cdot \dfrac{3 - 4i}{25} = \dfrac{25}{25} = 1\). \(z\) se multiply karke 1 aaya, yani yeh waqai \(1/z\) hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(\dfrac{1}{z} = \dfrac{\overline{z}}{|z|^{2}}\) (jab \(z \ne 0\)); yani reciprocal nikaalne ke liye conjugate ko modulus ke square se divide karein.

blocks.explanation: Yahan complex number ordered pair \((a, b)\) ki shakal mein diya gaya hai, jis ka matlab \(a + ib\) hai. Multiplicative inverse (ulta / reciprocal) woh pair hai jis se multiply karne par \((1, 0)\) mile, jo multiplication ka identity hai, bilkul jaise real numbers mein 5 ka inverse \(1/5\) hai kyun ke \(5 \times 1/5 = 1\). Formula (jo Sawal 3(iv) se hi nikalta hai): \((a, b)^{-1} = \left(\frac{a}{a^2 + b^2}, \frac{-b}{a^2 + b^2}\right)\). Plan: \(a\) aur \(b\) pehchanein, \(a^2 + b^2\) nikaalein, formula mein daalein, aur aakhir mein multiply karke check karein.
steps:
Step 1: \(a\) aur \(b\) pehchanein
\[a = -4, \quad b = 7\]
Kyun: Ordered pair \((a, b)\) mein pehla number \(a\) (real part) aur doosra \(b\) (imaginary part) hai. Yani yeh number \(-4 + 7i\) hai.

Step 2: \(a^2 + b^2\) nikaalein
\[(-4)^{2} + 7^{2} = 16 + 49\]
\[= 65\]
Kyun: Formula ke dono hisson ke neeche yahi aata hai, is liye pehle isay nikaal lena aasaan hai. Negative number ka square positive hota hai: \((-4)^2 = +16\).

Step 3: Formula mein values daalein
\[\left(\dfrac{-4}{65}, \dfrac{-7}{65}\right)\]
Kyun: Pehla hissa \(a/65 = -4/65\). Doosre hisse mein \(-b\) aata hai: \(-b = -7\), to \(-7/65\).
Dhyan dein: Formula mein sirf \(b\) ka sign badalta hai, \(a\) ka nahin. Bohat se students dono signs badal dete hain.

Tasdeeq: \((-4, 7)\) se multiply karein
Formula \((a, b)(c, d) = (ac - bd, ad + bc)\) use karein.
\[ac - bd = \tfrac{16}{65} + \tfrac{49}{65} = 1\]
\[ad + bc = \tfrac{28}{65} - \tfrac{28}{65} = 0\]
Product \((1, 0)\) aaya, jo identity hai. Jawab theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(\left(\dfrac{-4}{65}, \dfrac{-7}{65}\right)\) (is pair ko \((-4, 7)\) se multiply karein to \((1, 0)\) milta hai)

blocks.explanation: Part (i) wala hi tareeqa aur wahi formula, lekin yahan do cheezon ka khaas khayal rakhna hai: square roots, aur \(b\) ka apna minus sign. Formula ke doosre hisse mein \(-b\) aata hai, aur yahan \(b\) khud negative hai, to minus ka minus plus ban jayega. Plan: \(a\) aur \(b\) pehchanein, \(a^2 + b^2\) nikaalein, formula mein daalein, multiply karke check karein.
steps:
Step 1: \(a\) aur \(b\) pehchanein
\[a = \sqrt{2}, \quad b = -\sqrt{5}\]
Kyun: Pair ka pehla number \(a\) aur doosra \(b\). Minus sign \(b\) ka hissa hai, isay \(b\) ke saath hi rakhein.

Step 2: \(a^2 + b^2\) nikaalein
\[(\sqrt{2})^{2} + (-\sqrt{5})^{2}\]
\[= 2 + 5 = 7\]
Kyun: Square root ka square andar wala number deta hai: \((\sqrt{2})^2 = 2\). Aur negative ka square positive, is liye \((-\sqrt{5})^2 = +5\).

Step 3: Formula mein daalein
\[-b = -(-\sqrt{5}) = \sqrt{5}\]
\[\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{7}, \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{7}\right)\]
Kyun: Pehla hissa \(a/7 = \sqrt{2}/7\). Doosra hissa \(-b/7\), aur \(-b = +\sqrt{5}\), is liye \(+\sqrt{5}/7\).
Dhyan dein: Yahan \(-\sqrt{5}/7\) likhna sab se aam ghalti hai. Pehle \(-b\) alag line mein nikaalein, phir likhein.

Tasdeeq: \((\sqrt{2}, -\sqrt{5})\) se multiply karein
\[ac - bd = \tfrac{2}{7} + \tfrac{5}{7} = 1\]
\[ad + bc = \tfrac{\sqrt{10}}{7} - \tfrac{\sqrt{10}}{7} = 0\]
Product \((1, 0)\) aaya. Jawab theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{7}, \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{7}\right)\) (doosre hisse ka sign palat gaya, kyun ke formula mein \(-b\) hai)

blocks.explanation: Yeh pehchaniye: \((1, 0)\) asal mein complex number \(1 + 0i = 1\) hai, jo khud multiplication ka identity hai. Andaza lagayein to jawab yahi hona chahiye, kyun ke real numbers mein bhi 1 ka inverse 1 hai. Lekin exam mein andaza nahin, hisaab dikhana hota hai, is liye formula laga kar dekhte hain aur check bhi karte hain.
steps:
Step 1: \(a\) aur \(b\) pehchanein
\[a = 1, \quad b = 0\]
\[a^{2} + b^{2} = 1\]
Kyun: Pair ka pehla number 1 aur doosra 0 hai; \(1^2 + 0^2 = 1\).

Step 2: Formula mein daalein
\[\left(\dfrac{1}{1}, \dfrac{-0}{1}\right) = (1, 0)\]
Kyun: Pehla hissa \(1/1 = 1\). Doosra hissa \(-0/1\), aur \(-0 = 0\) hi hai, zero ka koi sign nahin hota.

Tasdeeq:
\[(1, 0)(1, 0) = (1 - 0, \, 0 + 0)\]
\[= (1, 0)\]
Jaise real number 1 ka inverse 1 hi hai, waise hi \((1, 0)\) apna inverse khud hai. Hamara andaza bhi sahi nikla.
blocks.final_answer: \((1, 0)\) (identity apna inverse khud hai)

blocks.prompt: 5 (i) Separate into real and imaginary parts (write as a simple complex number): \(\dfrac{2 - 7i}{4 + 5i}\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh complex numbers ki division ka sawal hai. Humein jawab \(x + iy\) ki simple shakal mein likhna hai, jis ke neeche koi \(i\) na ho. Problem yeh hai ke denominator \(4 + 5i\) mein \(i\) hai. Is ka ilaaj: upar neeche denominator ke conjugate se multiply karein, kyun ke \((c + id)(c - id) = c^2 + d^2\) hamesha real hota hai (Sawal 3(iii) yaad karein). Yahan \(4 + 5i\) ka conjugate \(4 - 5i\) hai. Plan: multiply, upar expand, neeche simplify, phir real aur imaginary parts alag.
steps:
Step 1: Denominator ke conjugate se multiply karein
\[\dfrac{2 - 7i}{4 + 5i} \cdot \dfrac{4 - 5i}{4 - 5i}\]
Kyun: \((4 - 5i)/(4 - 5i) = 1\), is liye value wahi rehti hai, lekin neeche se \(i\) khatam ho jayega.
Dhyan dein: Conjugate hamesha denominator ka lein, numerator ka nahin.

Step 2: Upar (numerator) expand karein
\[(2 - 7i)(4 - 5i)\]
\[= 8 - 10i - 28i + 35i^{2}\]
\[= 8 - 38i - 35\]
\[= -27 - 38i\]
Kyun: Har term ko har term se multiply kiya: \(2 \cdot 4 = 8\), \(2 \cdot (-5i) = -10i\), \((-7i) \cdot 4 = -28i\), \((-7i)(-5i) = 35i^2\). Phir \(i^2 = -1\) lagaya to \(35i^2 = -35\), aur real parts \(8 - 35 = -27\).

Step 3: Neeche (denominator) nikaalein
\[(4 + 5i)(4 - 5i) = 16 - 25i^{2}\]
\[= 16 + 25 = 41\]
Kyun: \((x + y)(x - y) = x^2 - y^2\) ka formula, aur \(i^2 = -1\) ki wajah se \(-25i^2 = +25\). Shortcut: neeche hamesha \(c^2 + d^2 = 16 + 25\) aata hai.

Step 4: Real aur imaginary parts alag karein
\[\dfrac{-27 - 38i}{41} = -\dfrac{27}{41} - \dfrac{38}{41}i\]
Kyun: Upar ke dono hisson ko alag alag 41 se divide kiya, taake jawab \(x + iy\) ki shakal mein aa jaye.

Tasdeeq:
\[(-27 - 38i)(4 + 5i)\]
\[= -108 - 135i - 152i - 190i^{2}\]
\[= 82 - 287i = 41(2 - 7i)\]
Yani jawab \(\times (4 + 5i) = 2 - 7i\), jo asal numerator hai. Theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(-\dfrac{27}{41} - \dfrac{38}{41}i\); real part \(-\dfrac{27}{41}\), imaginary part \(-\dfrac{38}{41}\) (dono parts negative, yani point teesre quadrant mein hai)

blocks.prompt: 5 (ii) Separate into real and imaginary parts (write as a simple complex number): \(\dfrac{(-2 + 3i)^{2}}{1 + i}\).
blocks.explanation: Is sawal mein do kaam hain, aur tarteeb aham hai. Pehle numerator mein \((-2 + 3i)^2\) hai; jab tak isay expand karke aik simple complex number na bana lein, division saaf tareeqe se nahin hogi. Phir denominator \(1 + i\) hai, jis ka conjugate \(1 - i\) hai. Plan: square expand karein, phir conjugate se multiply karein, phir parts alag karein.
steps:
Step 2: Denominator ke conjugate se multiply karein
\[\dfrac{-5 - 12i}{1 + i} \cdot \dfrac{1 - i}{1 - i}\]
Kyun: \(1 + i\) ka conjugate \(1 - i\) hai; is se neeche real number aa jayega aur value nahin badlegi.

Step 3: Upar expand karein
\[(-5 - 12i)(1 - i)\]
\[= -5 + 5i - 12i + 12i^{2}\]
\[= -5 - 7i - 12\]
\[= -17 - 7i\]
Kyun: \((-5)(-i) = +5i\) aur \((-12i)(-i) = 12i^2 = -12\). Minus ko minus se multiply karte waqt signs ka khaas khayal rakhein.

Step 4: Neeche nikaalein
\[(1 + i)(1 - i) = 1 - i^{2} = 2\]
Kyun: Difference of squares, aur \(-i^2 = +1\), to \(1 + 1 = 2\).

Step 5: Parts alag karein
\[\dfrac{-17 - 7i}{2} = -\dfrac{17}{2} - \dfrac{7}{2}i\]
Kyun: Dono hisson ko alag alag 2 se divide kiya, taake jawab \(x + iy\) shakal mein ho.
blocks.final_answer: \(-\dfrac{17}{2} - \dfrac{7}{2}i\); real part \(-\dfrac{17}{2}\), imaginary part \(-\dfrac{7}{2}\)

blocks.prompt: 5 (iii) Separate into real and imaginary parts (write as a simple complex number): \(\dfrac{i}{1 + i}\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh chhota sa division hai: upar sirf \(i\) hai aur neeche \(1 + i\). Neeche \(i\) maujood hai, is liye simple shakal ke liye usay hataana hoga. Wahi purana tareeqa: upar neeche denominator ke conjugate \(1 - i\) se multiply karein, phir real aur imaginary parts alag kar dein.
steps:
Step 1: Conjugate se multiply karein
\[\dfrac{i}{1 + i} \cdot \dfrac{1 - i}{1 - i}\]
Kyun: \((1 - i)/(1 - i) = 1\), value badle baghair neeche se \(i\) nikal jata hai.

Step 2: Upar aur neeche
\[i(1 - i) = i - i^{2} = 1 + i\]
\[(1 + i)(1 - i) = 2\]
Kyun: Upar \(i\) ko bracket ke dono terms se multiply kiya: \(i \cdot 1 = i\) aur \(i \cdot (-i) = -i^2 = +1\). Neeche wahi hai jo part (ii) mein aaya tha: \(1 - i^2 = 2\).

Step 3: Parts alag karein
\[\dfrac{1 + i}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}i\]
Kyun: Dono hisson ko 2 se divide kiya. Real part \(1/2\) aur imaginary part bhi \(1/2\).

Tasdeeq:
\[\tfrac{1}{2}(1 + i)(1 + i) = \tfrac{1}{2}(2i) = i\]
Jawab ko \((1 + i)\) se multiply karke wapas \(i\) mil gaya. Theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}i\); real part \(\dfrac{1}{2}\), imaginary part \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) (dono parts barabar hain)

blocks.prompt: 5 (iv) Separate into real and imaginary parts (write as a simple complex number): \(\dfrac{(4 + 3i)^{2}}{4 - 3i}\).
blocks.explanation: Yeh part (ii) jaisa hai: pehle numerator ka square \((4 + 3i)^2\) expand karna hai, phir division. Denominator \(4 - 3i\) hai, aur is ka conjugate \(4 + 3i\) hai (sirf \(i\) wale hisse ka sign badla). Dilchasp baat yeh hai ke conjugate wahi number nikla jo upar square mein hai, lekin hum phir bhi qadam ba qadam chalenge. Plan: square expand karein, conjugate se multiply karein, upar neeche simplify karein, parts alag karein.
steps:
Step 2: Conjugate se multiply karein
\[\dfrac{7 + 24i}{4 - 3i} \cdot \dfrac{4 + 3i}{4 + 3i}\]
Kyun: \(4 - 3i\) ka conjugate \(4 + 3i\) hai. Is se neeche real number aayega aur value wahi rahegi.
Dhyan dein: Conjugate mein sirf imaginary part ka sign badalta hai; \(4\) ko \(-4\) mat banayein.

Step 4: Neeche nikaalein
\[(4 - 3i)(4 + 3i) = 16 - 9i^{2}\]
\[= 16 + 9 = 25\]
Kyun: Difference of squares formula, aur \(-9i^2 = +9\). Yaad rakhiye: neeche hamesha \(c^2 + d^2\) aata hai, yahan \(4^2 + 3^2 = 25\).

Step 5: Parts alag karein
\[\dfrac{-44 + 117i}{25} = -\dfrac{44}{25} + \dfrac{117}{25}i\]
Kyun: Dono hisson ko alag alag 25 se divide kiya.

Tasdeeq:
\[(-44 + 117i)(4 - 3i)\]
\[= -176 + 132i + 468i - 351i^{2}\]
\[= 175 + 600i = 25(7 + 24i)\]
Yani jawab \(\times (4 - 3i) = 7 + 24i\), jo expand kiya hua numerator hai. Theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(-\dfrac{44}{25} + \dfrac{117}{25}i\); real part \(-\dfrac{44}{25}\), imaginary part \(\dfrac{117}{25}\) (real part negative, imaginary positive: doosra quadrant)

blocks.prompt: 6 If \(z_1 = 2 + i\), \(z_2 = 3 - 2i\), \(z_3 = 1 + 3i\) then express \(\dfrac{\overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_3}}{z_2}\) in the form of \(a + ib\).
blocks.explanation: Sab se pehle dekhte hain ke given kya hai: teen complex numbers \(z_1 = 2 + i\), \(z_2 = 3 - 2i\), \(z_3 = 1 + 3i\). Find karna hai \(\overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_3}/z_2\), aur jawab \(a + ib\) shakal mein. Kitab mein \(z_1\) aur \(z_3\) dono par conjugate ki line (bar) hai, \(z_2\) par nahin. Plan: (1) dono conjugates likhein, (2) unhein multiply karke aik number banayein, (3) \(z_2\) se divide karein, yani upar neeche \(\overline{z_2}\) se multiply karein, (4) \(a + ib\) mein likhein. Aik tasalli ki baat: agar aik hi bar poore product par hota tab bhi jawab yahi aata, kyun ke \(\overline{z_1 z_3} = \overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_3}\).
steps:
Step 1: Conjugates likhein
\[\overline{z_1} = 2 - i\]
\[\overline{z_3} = 1 - 3i\]
Kyun: Conjugate mein real part wahi rehta hai aur imaginary part ka sign badal jata hai. \(z_2\) par bar nahin, is liye usay waisa hi rakhein.

Step 2: Conjugates multiply karein
\[(2 - i)(1 - 3i)\]
\[= 2 - 6i - i + 3i^{2}\]
\[= 2 - 7i - 3\]
\[= -1 - 7i\]
Kyun: Har term ko har term se: \(2 \cdot 1 = 2\), \(2(-3i) = -6i\), \((-i)(1) = -i\), \((-i)(-3i) = 3i^2 = -3\). Real parts \(2 - 3 = -1\), imaginary \(-6i - i = -7i\).

Step 3: \(z_2\) ke conjugate se multiply karein
\[\dfrac{-1 - 7i}{3 - 2i} \cdot \dfrac{3 + 2i}{3 + 2i}\]
Kyun: \(\overline{z_2} = 3 + 2i\) se upar neeche multiply karne se neeche real number ban jayega aur value nahin badlegi.
Dhyan dein: Yahan \(\overline{z_2}\) sirf division ka aala (tool) hai; sawal mein \(z_2\) ka conjugate nahin manga gaya. Is ko Step 1 ke conjugates se mix mat karein.

Step 5: Neeche nikaalein
\[(3 - 2i)(3 + 2i) = 9 - 4i^{2}\]
\[= 9 + 4 = 13\]
Kyun: Difference of squares; neeche hamesha \(c^2 + d^2 = 9 + 4\) aata hai.

Step 6: \(a + ib\) shakal mein likhein
\[\dfrac{11 - 23i}{13} = \dfrac{11}{13} - \dfrac{23}{13}i\]
Kyun: Dono hisson ko alag alag 13 se divide kiya, to \(a = 11/13\) aur \(b = -23/13\).

Tasdeeq:
\[\tfrac{1}{13}(11 - 23i)(3 - 2i)\]
\[= \tfrac{1}{13}(33 - 91i + 46i^{2})\]
\[= \tfrac{1}{13}(-13 - 91i)\]
\[= -1 - 7i\]
Jawab ko \(z_2\) se multiply karke wapas numerator \(-1 - 7i\) mil gaya. Theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(\dfrac{\overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_3}}{z_2} = \dfrac{11}{13} - \dfrac{23}{13}i\) (yani \(a = \dfrac{11}{13}\), \(b = -\dfrac{23}{13}\))

blocks.text: Sawal ka stem (jaisa kitab mein hai, durust kar ke): Agar \(z_1 = 2 + 7i\) aur \(z_2 = -5 + 3i\) hon, to neeche diye gaye expressions ki value nikaalein (evaluate karein). Charon hisson mein modulus nikaalna hai, aur tareeqa aik hi hai: pehle andar wala expression aik complex number banayein, phir modulus lein.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "the evaluate the following" chhapa hai; durust jumla "then evaluate the following" hai. Yeh sirf chhapai ki ghalti hai; sawal ke hisaab kitaab par is ka koi asar nahin.

blocks.explanation: Yahan modulus nikaalna hai. Modulus yaad karein: \(|a + ib| = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), yani origin se point ka faasla. Lekin yeh formula sirf aik number \(a + ib\) par lagta hai, poore expression \(2z_1 - 4z_2\) par seedha nahin. Is liye plan yeh hai: pehle \(2z_1 - 4z_2\) ko aik complex number banayein, phir us ka modulus lein, aur aakhir mein square root ko simplify karein.
steps:
Step 1: \(2z_1 - 4z_2\) nikaalein
\[2(2 + 7i) - 4(-5 + 3i)\]
\[= 4 + 14i + 20 - 12i\]
\[= 24 + 2i\]
Kyun: \(2\) ko \(z_1\) ke dono terms se multiply kiya, aur \(-4\) ko \(z_2\) ke dono terms se: \(-4 \times -5 = +20\) aur \(-4 \times 3i = -12i\). Phir real parts \(4 + 20 = 24\) aur imaginary parts \(14i - 12i = 2i\).
Dhyan dein: \(-4\) ka minus bracket ke dono terms par lagta hai; \(-4 \times -5\) ko \(-20\) likhna aam ghalti hai.

Step 2: Modulus lein
\[|24 + 2i| = \sqrt{24^{2} + 2^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{576 + 4} = \sqrt{580}\]
Kyun: Ab aik number \(24 + 2i\) hai, jahan \(a = 24\) aur \(b = 2\). Modulus mein \(i\) nahin aata, sirf \(b\) ka square.

Step 3: Root simplify karein
\[\sqrt{580} = \sqrt{4 \times 145}\]
\[= 2\sqrt{145}\]
Kyun: 580 ka sab se bara perfect square factor 4 hai: 580 = 4 x 145. \(\sqrt{4} = 2\) bahar aa jata hai. 145 = 5 x 29 mein koi aur square factor nahin, is liye yahin ruk jate hain.

Tasdeeq:
\[(2\sqrt{145})^{2} = 4 \times 145 = 580\]
Yeh \(24^2 + 2^2 = 580\) ke barabar hai. Jawab theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(|2z_1 - 4z_2| = 2\sqrt{145}\) (yani point \(24 + 2i\) origin se \(2\sqrt{145}\) ki doori par hai)

blocks.explanation: Wahi tareeqa jo part (i) mein tha: pehle andar ka expression aik number, phir modulus. Farq sirf yeh hai ke yahan \(z_1\) ka conjugate bhi aa gaya hai, to pehle usay likh lete hain: \(\overline{z_1} = 2 - 7i\). Plan: \(3z_1 + 2\overline{z_1}\) nikaalein, phir \(\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\) lagayein.
steps:
Step 1: \(3z_1 + 2\overline{z_1}\) nikaalein
\[3(2 + 7i) + 2(2 - 7i)\]
\[= 6 + 21i + 4 - 14i\]
\[= 10 + 7i\]
Kyun: Brackets kholein: \(3(2 + 7i) = 6 + 21i\) aur \(2(2 - 7i) = 4 - 14i\). Phir real parts \(6 + 4 = 10\) aur \(i\) wale parts \(21i - 14i = 7i\) alag alag jama kiye.

Step 2: Modulus lein
\[|10 + 7i| = \sqrt{10^{2} + 7^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{100 + 49} = \sqrt{149}\]
Kyun: \(a = 10\), \(b = 7\). 149 prime number hai (kisi chhote prime 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 se divide nahin hota), is liye is ka root mazeed simplify nahin hota.

Tasdeeq:
\(\sqrt{149}\) taqreeban 12.2 hai (kyun ke \(12^2 = 144\)). Yeh 10 aur 7 dono se bara hai lekin \(10 + 7 = 17\) se chhota, jo kisi triangle ke hypotenuse (kaan) ke liye bilkul munasib hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(|3z_1 + 2\overline{z_1}| = \sqrt{149}\) (149 prime hai, is liye yahi sab se simple shakal hai)

blocks.explanation: Yeh bhi wahi tareeqa hai, is baar \(z_2\) aur us ke conjugate ke saath. Pehle conjugate likh lein: \(z_2 = -5 + 3i\), to \(\overline{z_2} = -5 - 3i\) (real part \(-5\) waisa hi, sirf \(3i\) ka sign badla). Plan: \(-7z_2 + 2\overline{z_2}\) ko aik number banayein, phir modulus lein. Yahan negative numbers zyada hain, is liye signs par khaas nazar rakhni hai.
steps:
Step 1: \(-7z_2 + 2\overline{z_2}\) nikaalein
\[-7(-5 + 3i) + 2(-5 - 3i)\]
\[= 35 - 21i - 10 - 6i\]
\[= 25 - 27i\]
Kyun: \(-7 \times -5 = +35\) aur \(-7 \times 3i = -21i\); \(2 \times -5 = -10\) aur \(2 \times -3i = -6i\). Phir real parts \(35 - 10 = 25\) aur \(i\) parts \(-21i - 6i = -27i\).
Dhyan dein: Conjugate lete waqt \(-5\) ko \(+5\) mat banayein; sirf imaginary part ka sign badalta hai.

Step 2: Modulus lein
\[|25 - 27i| = \sqrt{25^{2} + (-27)^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{625 + 729}\]
\[= \sqrt{1354}\]
Kyun: \(a = 25\), \(b = -27\), aur \((-27)^2 = +729\), minus khatam. 1354 = 2 x 677, aur 677 prime hai, is liye koi square factor nahin aur root simplify nahin hota.

Tasdeeq:
Aam ghalti: \(b = -27\) ka square \(-729\) likh dena (calculator par bhi \(-27^2\) type karein to \(-729\) aata hai). Poore \(-27\) ka square \(+729\) hota hai, is liye bracket lagayein. Modulus kabhi negative ya zero se chhota nahin ho sakta, is liye jawab \(\sqrt{1354}\) hi hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(|-7z_2 + 2\overline{z_2}| = \sqrt{1354}\) (taqreeban 36.8)

blocks.explanation: Yahan cube ka modulus chahiye: \(|(z_1 + z_2)^3|\). Aik raasta yeh hai ke cube poora expand karein, lekin woh lamba hai aur ghalti ka imkaan zyada hai. Samajhdaar raasta: qanoon \(|z^n| = |z|^n\) (yeh \(|z_1 z_2| = |z_1||z_2|\) se nikalta hai). Yani pehle modulus lein, phir cube karein; jawab wahi aayega. Plan: \(z_1 + z_2\) nikaalein, us ka modulus lein, aur us ka cube karein. Aakhir mein tasdeeq ke liye lamba raasta bhi check kar lenge.
steps:
Step 1: \(z_1\) aur \(z_2\) add karein
\[(2 + 7i) + (-5 + 3i)\]
\[= -3 + 10i\]
Kyun: Real parts aapas mein (\(2 - 5 = -3\)) aur imaginary parts aapas mein (\(7i + 3i = 10i\)) jama kiye.

Step 2: \(|z^3| = |z|^3\) use karein
\[|(z_1 + z_2)^{3}| = |z_1 + z_2|^{3}\]
Kyun: \(z^3 = z \cdot z \cdot z\), aur product ka modulus moduli ka product hota hai: \(|z \cdot z \cdot z| = |z||z||z| = |z|^3\). Is se cube expand karne ki zaroorat khatam.

Step 4: Cube karein
\[(\sqrt{109})^{3} = \sqrt{109} \cdot \sqrt{109} \cdot \sqrt{109}\]
\[= 109\sqrt{109}\]
Kyun: Do roots aapas mein multiply ho kar 109 ban jate hain (\(\sqrt{109} \cdot \sqrt{109} = 109\)), aur aik root bach jata hai.
Dhyan dein: \((\sqrt{109})^3\) ko \(109^3\) ya \(3\sqrt{109}\) mat likhein; cube ka matlab teen baar multiply karna hai.

Tasdeeq: cube seedha expand karein
\[(-3 + 10i)^{3} = 873 - 730i\]
\[873^{2} + 730^{2} = 1295029\]
\[109^{3} = 1295029\]
Yani \(|873 - 730i| = \sqrt{109^3} = 109\sqrt{109}\). Lamba raasta bhi wahi jawab deta hai, to shortcut sahi tha.
blocks.final_answer: \(|(z_1 + z_2)^{3}| = 109\sqrt{109}\) (pehle modulus, phir cube: kaam bohat chhota ho gaya)
